messages.author: 066a0ceb2819d0e3
messages.subject: Incorrect output with summarise
parts:
There are some instances where summarise returns the first row of a column instead of the summary statistic.  I have created a minimal example using a data.frame of 3 x 47.  That data.frame has been attached to this email.

out2 <- read.table("out2.txt")
wf <- summarise(out2,
      IC_REITs = round(mean(IC2100), 4),
      IC = round(mean(IC), 4))
wf
mean(out2$IC)


> out2 <- read.table("out2.txt")
> wf <- summarise(out2,
+       IC_REITs = round(mean(IC2100), 4),
+       IC = round(mean(IC), 4))
> wf
  IC_REITs      IC
1        0 -0.2078
> mean(out2$IC)
[1] -0.08572147
>

If I take out the round() function it works fine:

> wf <- summarise(out2,
+                 IC_REITs = mean(IC2100),
+                 IC = mean(IC))
> wf
  IC_REITs          IC
1        0 -0.08572147
> mean(out2$IC)
[1] -0.08572147

The round() function is not the problem, however, it appears to be the () around it:

> wf <- summarise(out2,
+                 IC_REITs = (mean(IC2100)),
+                 IC = (mean(IC)))
> wf
  IC_REITs         IC
1        0 -0.2077565
> mean(out2$IC)
[1] -0.08572147
> mean(out2$IC)

Bizarrely, if we remove one unnecessary column it works fine:

> wf <- summarise(out2[, -5],
+                 IC_REITs = (mean(IC2100)),
+                 IC = (mean(IC)))
> wf
  IC_REITs          IC
1        0 -0.08572147
> mean(out2$IC)
[1] -0.08572147
